title: Architecture and Standards: API, Coding, Infra, Model-Serving, Observability, Performance
author: Sarah Kim
content:
Overview

This document codifies Redwood Inference's cross-cutting architecture and engineering standards: API design, code quality, infrastructure-as-code (IaC), model-serving, observability, and performance. It is intended to be the canonical reference for teams building services and model-serving components that must meet our production SLAs, security constraints, and operational expectations.

Scope

- Applies to all new services, major refactors, and model onboarding efforts across Hosted API, Dedicated, and Private deployments.
- Does not replace team-level design docs; it complements them by capturing company-wide minimums and recommended defaults.

Goals

1. Ensure consistent, secure, and discoverable APIs for internal and external clients.
2. Maintain high code quality and low cognitive overhead when reasoning about services.
3. Provide safe, repeatable infrastructure patterns using IaC.
4. Standardize model-serving lifecycle and fallbacks to protect customer availability.
5. Make services observable and debuggable with minimal toil.
6. Set measurable performance targets and testing guardrails.

Ownership and Governance

- Standards owner: Architecture & Standards guild (contact: sarah.kim@redwood.com).
- Change process: Propose ADR (see ADRs section) and open RFC PR in the architecture repo. Major changes require sign-off from eng-platform and eng-sre.

1) API Standards

Purpose: Create predictable, stable interfaces for SDKs, internal integrations, and external customers.

Key principles
- Design for clients first: simple payloads, clear error semantics, and forward/backward compatibility.
- Each public API must include machine-readable versioning metadata.
- Prefer HTTP/JSON REST for external APIs and gRPC for high-throughput internal control plane communication.

Naming and structure
- Use kebab-case for REST endpoints (e.g., POST /v1/runs, GET /v1/models/{model-id}/metrics).
- Plural resources (e.g., /v1/models, not /v1/model).

Versioning
- Major version in path: /v{MAJOR}/... . Only break compatibility on major version bumps.
- Minor/patch changes can be implemented via additive fields and feature flags.

Error model
- Use RFC 7807 problem+json for structured errors. Fields required: type, title, status, detail, request_id.
- Distinguish between client (4xx) and server (5xx) errors and include retryable hint: 'retryable': true|false.

Pagination and list APIs
- Standardize on cursor-based pagination. Response envelope must include: items, next_cursor, has_more, total_count (optional).

Idempotency and safety
- All non-idempotent operations (e.g., job creation) must accept an Idempotency-Key header and perform deduplication for at least 24 hours in our control plane.

Rate limiting
- Rate limits are applied per-API-key and described in API catalog. Return 429 with Retry-After and problem+json body.

Contracts and schemas
- All public payloads must have OpenAPI (3.1) schemas checked into the service repo. Generated client SDKs are built from these specs.

Security headers and authentication
- Bearer tokens (OAuth2-like) for hosted API, mTLS for internal service-to-service calls, and API keys for legacy integrations.
- Enforce TLS 1.2+ and HSTS on all external endpoints.

2) Coding Standards

Languages and tech stack
- Primary backend languages: Go (services, control plane), Python (inference tooling, evals), and Rust/C++ for performance-critical kernels in the runtime.
- Frontend: TypeScript + React for console and internal dashboards.

Style and linters
- Use gofmt/goimports and golangci-lint for Go.
- Black + isort + flake8 for Python.
- ESLint + Prettier for TypeScript.
- Enforce formatting and linting in CI pre-merge checks.

Testing and QA
- Unit tests required for all public functions; target >= 80% coverage for core services.
- Integration tests must run against ephemeral infra in CI (localstack or k8s-in-docker) for features touching cloud resources.
- Contract tests for APIs: consumer-driven contract tests (Pact or equivalent) for external-facing endpoints.

PR requirements
- Every PR must include: description, design rationale, test plan, and roll-back plan (if applicable).
- Small, focused PRs preferred; >500 LOC changes require architecture review.

Dependency management
- Dependabot (or equivalent) enabled with weekly updates for critical vulnerabilities.
- Avoid pinning to unmaintained libraries; upgrade cadence documented in repo readme.

Secrets and keys
- Never commit secrets. Use Vault/KMS and the team's secrets onboarding. Secret scanning required in CI.

3) Infrastructure Standards (IaC and Networking)

IaC patterns
- Terraform as the canonical IaC for cloud resources. Module registry maintained by eng-infra.
- One environment per workspace: prod, staging, dev. Shared modules for VPC, IAM, and monitoring.

Account and networking
- Use centralized cloud accounts for org-level resources. Customer-specific private deployments live in customer-managed VPCs.
- Network segmentation: control-plane, runtime, management. Enforce least privilege on peering and firewall rules.

Terraform conventions
- Use remote state with locking (e.g., S3 + DynamoDB).
- Modules must include examples, variables with descriptions, and outputs.

Deployments and change control
- GitOps for application manifests (kustomize/helm), with automated CI/CD pipelines.
- Changes to production infra require runbook and RFC; emergency infra changes follow on-call approval workflow.

Backing services and storage
- Use managed services where feasible (RDS/Aurora, DynamoDB, S3). For high-throughput KV caches, prefer Redis with clustering.

4) Model-Serving Standards

Packaging and model artifacts
- Store model artifacts in versioned object storage with immutable manifests. Include the following metadata: model version, quantization profile, tokenizer hash, training-data-tag (if allowed), and performance profile.

Quantization and kernels
- Quantization profiles must be validated on a representative eval set. Maintain a signed quantization-profile JSON checked into model registry.
- Runtime kernels selected via an automated compatibility matrix; manual overrides require ADR.

Inference API contract
- Models exposed through the unified Redwood API must conform to the standard model manifest and support: health check, metadata endpoint, streaming responses, and deterministic seeding (where applicable).

KV cache and prefix caching
- All stateful runtime nodes must expose cache metrics and eviction policies. Default prefix caching behavior: cache up to 128 tokens per prefix and 10k prefixes per model by default; teams may tune with approval.

Rollouts and fallbacks
- Canary: 5% initial traffic, monitor error rate, latency, and quality signals for 30 minutes before progressing.
- Fallback policy: on load or increased error rate, automatically fallback to nearest compatible model variant (e.g., full->quantized or regional replica). Fallbacks must be tested in staging.

Observability and evals for quality
- Each model must include a small reference prompt set and automated quality checks deployed in CI. Regression alerts tied to evaluation thresholds (see Observability).

5) Observability Standards

Metrics
- Use OpenTelemetry for tracing and metrics. Metrics must be emitted with the following tags: service, route/model, region, host, environment.
- Required metrics (per-service): requests_total, requests_success, requests_error, latency_p50/p90/p99, tokens_generated_total, cache_hit_ratio.

Tracing and logs
- Instrument critical paths with distributed traces and a sampling policy: 100% traces for errors, 10% for successful high-latency requests.
- Structured logs (JSON) with request_id, user_id (if allowed), model_id, step, and severity. Logs retained per policy in security-and-compliance.

Dashboards and alerting
- Standard dashboards: Overview (SLOs), Traffic & Latency, Errors & Retries, Model Quality. Templates live in eng-platform.
- Alerts: Error rate > 1% for 5 minutes (P1), latency_p90 exceeding SLO for 10 minutes (P2). Alert thresholds defined in SLOs.

SLOs and Error budgets
- Services must define SLOs for availability and latency (examples below). Error budgets reviewed weekly by on-call.

6) Performance Standards and Benchmarks

SLO examples
- Hosted API generation endpoint: availability 99.9% (monthly), latency <= 300ms p50, <= 800ms p95 for 32-token responses under normal load.
- Dedicated inference pool: target throughput per GPU documented in model performance profile; 99.5% job completion SLA under reserved capacity.

Benchmarking and acceptance criteria
- Every model onboarding requires a perf benchmark report including: latency by sequence length, throughput at target batch sizes, memory usage, and cost-per-token estimates.
- Load testing: must include steady-state soak (4 hours at expected 2x peak) and spike tests. Results stored in the performance registry.

Performance tuning guidance
- Defaults: enable continuous batching, set max_batch_size per model based on perf profile, enable KV caching for long-prefix workloads.
- Quantization tradeoffs: list of recommended profiles and expected latency/cost impact must be recorded in the model manifest.

7) Decision Records (ADRs)

Process
- Use ADRs for all cross-cutting architectural decisions. ADR template resides in the architecture repo. Filename format: 000n-description.md.
- ADRs must include: context, decision, alternatives considered, consequences, and roll-back plan.

Example ADR index (recent)
- ADR-001: API versioning strategy (major-path-based) — accepted 2024-05-14
- ADR-014: Standardize on OpenTelemetry for tracing — accepted 2025-01-20
- ADR-021: Default quantization profiles and runtime kernel selection — in_review 2026-01-12

8) Implementation checklist (minimum required per new service or model)

- [ ] Open API spec checked in and validated.
- [ ] API contract tests added.
- [ ] Linting and formatting CI gates configured.
- [ ] Integration tests against ephemeral infra.
- [ ] Terraform modules and remote state workspace created.
- [ ] Observability: metrics, traces, and dashboard template added.
- [ ] SLOs documented and alert rules created.
- [ ] Performance benchmark report (for model-serving) uploaded.
- [ ] ADR opened for any non-standard deviation.

Appendix: Example snippets

OpenAPI header example:

  POST /v1/runs
  Content-Type: application/json
  Authorization: Bearer <token>
  Idempotency-Key: <uuid>

Problem+JSON example:

  {
    "type": "https://redwood.internal/errors/rate-limit",
    "title": "Rate limit exceeded",
    "status": 429,
    "detail": "Exceeded 100 requests per minute",
    "request_id": "req_123456",
    "retryable": true
  }

Telemetry metric name conventions (examples):
- redwood.requests.total
- redwood.requests.latency.p95
- redwood.model.tokens.generated_total
- redwood.cache.hit_ratio

Revision notes
- This is the canonical, company-wide standard. Teams may extend these standards in their team-level docs but must document deviations via an ADR and retain owner sign-off.
